newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-NZ BANS VENTER FOR RECKLESS STAMPING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NZ BANS VENTER FOR RECKLESS STAMPING.

text.p: A New Zealand rugby union judicial committee on Sunday suspended South African flanker Andre Venter for three-weeks for stamping on the head of All Black captain Sean Fitzpatrick during a Tri-Nations test.
Venter received the first red card of the series, being sent off by Welsh referee Derek Bevan for stamping on the face of the New Zealand captain in Saturday's test at Auckland.

The judicial committee appointed by series organisers SANZAR accepted Venter's claim that the incident was an accident, but found him guilty of reckless stamping and suspended him for three weeks, up to and including September 1.
A statement from the committee said it had obtained evidence from videotapes, Bevan and French touch judge Joel Dume.

"The judicial committee was not comfortably satisfied that Venter wilfully stamped on the head of the New Zealand player, but found he was engaged in reckless stamping as he entered the ruck, and in the course of that conduct made contact with the New Zealand player's head."
The three-week suspension is consistent with SANZAR's regulations drawn up by the three nations involved in the competition.

"The committee took into account the circumstances in which the player was sent off, the effect it had on his team and the public humiliation involved in being sent off in an international test match viewed by millions of people around the world," the statement said.
The South Africans may consider an appeal but had yet to view the full judgement from the committee, coach Carel du Plessis said before the Springboks flew out of Auckland.

"We thought his sending off was a bit harsh and now he's banned for three weeks. We won't have our flankers in Pretoria, which makes things even more difficult," du Plessis said of their August 23 match against the Wallabies.

South Africa's record 35-55 loss to New Zealand in Auckland means it is now impossible for them to win the Tri-Nations championship. New Zealand head the competition and next play Australia in Dunedin on Saturday.
